root_cause.text: The nft_ct timeout object was freed with plain kfree() in nft_ct_timeout_obj_destroy() immediately after nf_ct_untimeout(), even though other CPUs could still access the same nf_ct_timeout via RCU-protected rcu_dereference() lookups in nf_ct_timeout_data().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `struct rcu_head rcu;` to `struct nf_ct_timeout` and changes `kfree(priv->timeout);` to `kfree_rcu(priv->timeout, rcu);`, and the CVE description explicitly says concurrent packet processing may still hold RCU-protected references when the object is destroyed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an RCU callback field to nf_ct_timeout so it can be safely released or managed with RCU.
intent_record.what: A new `struct rcu_head rcu;` field was added to `struct nf_ct_timeout` between the existing `l4proto` pointer and the trailing `data[]` flexible array member.
intent_record.how: This change makes `nf_ct_timeout` objects compatible with RCU-based deferred freeing or cleanup, allowing the structure to participate in RCU lifecycle management at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Delay freeing nft_ct timeout state with RCU to avoid use-after-free during object destruction.
intent_record.what: In nft_ct_timeout_obj_destroy(), the call that frees priv->timeout was changed from kfree(priv->timeout) to kfree_rcu(priv->timeout, rcu).
intent_record.how: The timeout object is now freed after an RCU grace period instead of immediately, preventing use-after-free races when other RCU readers may still access the object during teardown.
